set.n: James Webster's forgotten buried money, Clay Township near Steamboat Rock
set.pl: Township-level: 1897 accounts put the farm in Clay Township, 'four miles from Eldora', and his obituary says he settled on a farm near Steamboat Rock in 1876. Pin in Clay Township between Steamboat Rock and the Eldora side, 5 km ring; farm not yet placed on a plat
set.st: James H. Webster, an Indiana man who went to the California gold rush in 1852, settled on a farm near Steamboat Rock in 1876. In May 1897 the Steamboat Rock Echo reported that he distrusted banks, had buried about $1,000 of pension money and several hundred dollars more, and then forgot the spot; searching failed. Wire copies that spring inflated it to $50,000 in casks. He was judged insane that spring and died in the state hospital at Independence in August 1897, leaving several thousand dollars of property. A dowser wrote to the probate judge offering to find his money. No find was reported.
set.t: The local amount (about $1,000-1,500) is the believable one. One local source (the editor 'can not vouch'); his obituary adds that he was said to carry considerable money on his person, which may mean some of it was never buried. Place Webster's farm in Clay Township on an 1890s Hardin plat. Access: private: permission.
